title: Expose cache telemetry config flags (enablement + sampling) and document defaults
author: Thomas Baird
release_notes:
- Adds runtime config flags to enable/disable cache telemetry and tune sampling/rate-limits per environment
- Documents recommended defaults for staging/canary/prod and how to roll out safely
commits: runtime/config: add CacheTelemetryConfig with env overrides
runtime/metrics: gate cache counters/histograms behind config
runtime/telemetry: add token-bucket rate limiter for cache event annotations
docs: update internal config reference + rollout guidance
description:
Context
We’re landing new prefix/KV cache telemetry (hit/miss, eviction/pressure, wasted prefill) across a series of PRs. SRE/Telemetry requested explicit runtime-side flags so we can (a) gate rollout per env and (b) dial sampling/rate limiting without code changes.

This PR introduces a single, typed config surface for cache telemetry and updates the internal runtime config docs with recommended defaults + rollout notes.

What’s in this PR
- New runtime config block: cache_telemetry
  - cache_telemetry.enabled (bool): global kill switch for all new cache telemetry emissions
  - cache_telemetry.metrics_enabled (bool): metrics-only gate (allows traces off/on separately)
  - cache_telemetry.traces_enabled (bool): enables span annotations for cache events (kept off by default in prod)
  - cache_telemetry.sample_rate (float 0.0–1.0): sampling for high-volume counters/histograms where we’ve approved sampling (implementation uses probabilistic sampling at request start)
  - cache_telemetry.event_rate_limit_per_sec (int): per-process token bucket for cache event annotations (primarily traces) to avoid bursty cost
  - cache_telemetry.emit_miss_reason_breakdown (bool): gate for miss reason label emission (kept on in staging/canary; prod default on with allowlist enforcement handled elsewhere)
- Wiring
  - All new cache metrics introduced in pr-18421/pr-18422/pr-18423/pr-18424 are now guarded by CacheTelemetryConfig checks.
  - Tracing annotations (added in a later PR) are prepared to use traces_enabled + event_rate_limit_per_sec.
  - Config is read once at runtime init; no hot reload in this PR (intentional to avoid partial-tag mismatches).
- Defaults
  - staging: enabled=true, metrics_enabled=true, traces_enabled=true, sample_rate=1.0, event_rate_limit_per_sec=500
  - canary: enabled=true, metrics_enabled=true, traces_enabled=false, sample_rate=0.25, event_rate_limit_per_sec=200
  - prod: enabled=true, metrics_enabled=true, traces_enabled=false, sample_rate=0.05, event_rate_limit_per_sec=100
  - NOTE: these defaults are conservative for prod; we can raise sample_rate once we confirm series cost with the ingestion-side cardinality guards.
- Docs
  - Adds a short “How to roll out cache telemetry safely” section that aligns with SRE canary gates: enable in staging -> enable in perf-canary at 25% sample -> prod at 5% sample -> tune.
  - Documents which signals are sampled vs unsampled (eviction pressure gauges remain unsampled).

Why this approach
- One top-level kill switch is necessary for incident response (telemetry cost spikes, unexpected overhead).
- Separating metrics_enabled vs traces_enabled matches how we control cost/cardinality: metrics are heavily constrained; traces can still get expensive quickly if enabled broadly.
- Keeping config read-only at startup avoids “mixed config” within a process that could produce confusing partial-series.

Testing
- Unit tests validate config parsing/validation (sample_rate bounds, negative rate limits, default application).
- Local load test sanity: toggling enabled=false removes all new cache series.
- Perf smoke runs included for instrumentation off/on at 5% sample (see CI).

Rollout
- Intended to ship before enabling cache telemetry in prod. Oncall can flip enabled=false via runtime config push if we see unexpected cost/overhead.

Links
- Linear: ENG-4821 (definitions/tags), ENG-4822 (runtime instrumentation)
- Related PRs: pr-18425 (sampling + rate limits), pr-18431 (naming reconciliation)

Open questions (not blocking)
- Do we want hot reload for sample_rate only? SRE asked for it, but it’s easy to introduce partial-series; proposing we revisit once ingestion drop detection is in place.

Reviewer notes / conversation summary
- Omar El-Sayed: requested that “enabled=false” must be a hard guarantee (no side-channel emissions). Author: updated guards to short-circuit before any miss-reason computation and added a regression test asserting zero increments.
- Nadia Rahman: asked to clarify which metrics are sampled and to avoid naming drift vs observability standards. Author: updated docs and aligned the config key names to match other telemetry blocks.
- Caleb Johnson: flagged risk of operators raising sample_rate without considering cardinality budgets. Author: added comments in defaults YAML + a doc callout that sample_rate > 0.25 requires ingestion guard verification.
- Marcus Reed: requested perf evidence that the flag checks don’t regress hot path. Author: ensured checks are branch-predictable and cached; posted perf smoke numbers in CI comment.
- Allison Grant: asked for explicit runbook snippet (“what knob to turn when dashboards go flat vs when cost spikes”). Author: added a small section to ops/runbooks/cache-telemetry-rollout.md.

Merge
Squash merged to main after CI green and approvals from Runtime + Telemetry + SRE.
